html:
The Multnomah were a Chinookan people on the lower Columbia River, centred on Sauvie Island near today's Portland, Oregon. Their villages of cedar plank houses held many people, fed by salmon, sturgeon and the wapato root.

They were part of the trading world of the Chinookan peoples, which linked the coast and the interior along the river. The Lewis and Clark Expedition passed their villages in 1805 and 1806. From 1830 a fever, probably malaria, swept the lower Columbia for several years and killed most of the Multnomah. Survivors joined other groups such as the Clackamas, and their descendants are among the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde. Portland's Multnomah County keeps their name.
